info.title: 1Platform API
info.description:
# 1Platform API

REST API powering the **1Platform** platform — content generation, SEO tooling, billing, invoicing, and third-party integrations.

---

## Authentication

1Platform uses a **two-token** authentication model:

| Token | Header | How to obtain | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------------|---------|
| **App token** | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `POST /api/v1/auth/token` with your App API key | Identifies the calling application |
| **User token** | `x-user-token: <token>` | `POST /api/v1/users/token` with the user API key | Identifies the end user |

Most endpoints require **both** tokens. Exceptions are noted per endpoint.

## Quickstart

```bash
# 1. Get an app token
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/auth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "ak-your-app-api-key"}'

# 2. Get a user token (requires app token)
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "sk-user-api-key"}'

# 3. Call any protected endpoint (requires both tokens)
curl https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/profile \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN"
```

## Base URL

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1/`.

## Rate Limits

| Category | Limit |
|----------|-------|
| Health | 100 req/min |
| Auth | 10 req/min |
| Read operations | 50 req/min |
| Write operations | 20 req/min |
| Keyword generation | 10 req/min |
| Content generation | 5 req/min |
| Indexing | 20 req/min |
| Agent runs | 10 req/min |
| Agent wizard | 20 req/min |
| Agent CRUD | 30 req/min |
| Agent metrics | 10 req/min |
| Client logs | 10 req/min |
| Analytics reads | 30 req/min |
| Analytics writes | 10 req/min |
| Analytics reports | 20 req/min |
| Analytics realtime | 10 req/min |
| Analytics events | 10 req/min |

## Response Format

All endpoints return a standard wrapper (except webhooks):

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": { ... },
  "msg": "Operation completed successfully"
}
```

get.description:
Returns the current health status of the API and its dependencies (database connectivity, etc.).

- **Auth:** None required
- **Rate limit:** 100 req/min

post.description:
Authenticate with an App API key and receive a JWT app token.

- **Auth:** None — this is the entry point for obtaining tokens
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min
- The returned `access_token` must be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on all protected endpoints
- Token expires after the time indicated in `expires_in` (seconds)

get.description:
List the authenticated user's generated articles — i.e. completed content-generation jobs — newest first. Powers the dashboard 'articles published' KPI, which buckets `created_at` by month.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min

Items are capped at the 1000 most recent; `total` is the exact count.

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN"
```

post.description:
Analyze a domain and extract SEO keywords using AI-powered search analysis. Requires an active App with an AI provider configured.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min

**Process:**
1. Analyzes domain content and structure
2. Extracts relevant keywords via search providers
3. Uses 1Platform AI to detect keyword cannibalization
4. Categorizes keywords by search intent and volume
5. Returns structured keyword data with metrics

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/posts/keywords/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"domain": "example.com", "country": "es", "lang": "en"}'
```

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`

2. Searches related content using search providers

4. Fetches relevant images from the configured image library
5. Creates a URL-friendly slug
6. Classifies content into provided categories

```bash
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

```

Run the site's setup again and refresh its status.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Free: nothing is charged.
- Safe to repeat: steps that already succeeded are skipped, so nothing is created twice and no email is sent again.
- A site that is already working is never downgraded by a failed check.

Add or verify a website in the link-building marketplace.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Actions:** `add` (register website) or `verify` (confirm ownership)
- The user must have marketplace credentials configured
- After adding, verify ownership to activate the listing

post.description:
Add, verify, delete a website or manage sitemaps in Google Search Console.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Actions:** `add`, `verify`, `delete`, `sitemaps`
- The website must be registered in the platform before adding to Search Console
- For `sitemaps` action, include a `payload.sitemaps` array with sitemap URLs
- `sitemaps` requires ownership to be verified first; before that it returns 412 without charging
- `add` accepts an optional `verification_method` (`FILE`, the default, or `META`). `META` is only available for sites 1Platform serves, because it publishes the tag on the site itself; asking for it on any other site returns 409 without charging.
- Requires a Google service account with Search Console access

get.description:
Retrieve a Search Console performance report for a verified website: 4 KPIs (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position) with a delta vs. the immediately preceding period of equal length, a daily trend, and the top 25 queries/pages/countries.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Free** — unlike add/verify/delete/sitemaps, this is a read-only report and is never charged
- Served from the figures 1Platform has stored, refreshed periodically in the background; `last_synced_at` says when. A site that has never been synchronised is loaded on this first request and answers a little slower
- Requires the website to already be verified in Search Console (409 otherwise)

get.summary: Search the WordPress plugin directory / check abandonment
get.description:
One endpoint behind one cache-aside provider (D-8/D-9): with `q`, a text search against the directory for WPG-10's install dialog, each hit flagged with whether it is already on this site; without `q`, `abandoned` maps the site's OWN currently-reported plugin slugs to the directory's last release date, for every one that crossed the configured maintenance window (WPG-09). A directory outage degrades to empty results / an empty map, never a 500.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min

patch.summary: Enable, disable, or apportion automatic catalog publishing for a website (ACA-05)
patch.description:
Turn automatic publishing on/off for a website served by a 1Platform tenant (Atlas), and set its monthly budget / catalog kinds / item cap.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Only the website owner can change it
- The website must already be served by a tenant (`atlas_tenant_slug` set), otherwise this responds `409 WEBSITE_NOT_A_TENANT`
- `unit_price_usd_override` cannot be set here — it is superadmin-only via `PATCH /platform/websites/{id}/autopublish/price`; sending it responds `422 AUTOPUBLISH_FIELD_NOT_WRITABLE` and applies nothing

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/websites/<WEBSITE_ID>/autopublish \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": true, "kinds": ["book"], "monthly_budget_usd": "5.00", "max_items_per_cycle": 200}'
```

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`

Generate a complete profile card for a person using AI.

- Includes gender detection, bio generation, social media discovery, and profile image retrieval
- Provide the person's name as `owner`; optional `context` enriches the bio

post.description:
Revoke all existing JWT tokens for the authenticated user.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min
- Increments the user's `token_version`, invalidating all previously issued tokens
- After calling this endpoint, the user must obtain a new token via `POST /api/v1/users/token`

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/revoke-tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN"
```

get.description:
Every credential issued to the caller, masked. The secret is never here: it is shown once, when it is issued, and only its hash is kept.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

post.description:
Issues a personal user token and returns its secret **once**. There is no endpoint that returns it again — only its hash is stored.

Requires API Developer to be granted to the caller.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

201.description: Credential created — the secret is in this response and nowhere else

post.summary: Reveal an approved app token, once
post.description:
Generates the secret of a token an administrator approved and returns it. It exists nowhere before this call — which is how the administrator who granted it is unable to see it — and only its hash exists afterwards.

Only the assigned user can call this. A second call is a 409.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

200.description: Revealed — the secret is in this response and nowhere else

patch.description:
Cuts the credential's access on the next request, including for a token already issued from it. Idempotent.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

delete.description:
Logical delete: it disappears from the listing, frees a slot against the ceiling and stops authenticating, while the record of who created it and when it was last used survives. Answers a body, never 204.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

get.description:
Everything the panel needs to decide what to show: whether access is granted, the latest request if there is one, and whether an approved token is still waiting to be revealed.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

post.description:
Creates a request for an administrator of the workspace to review, and notifies them.

Idempotent while one is pending: asking again returns the existing request with 200 and sends nothing, so tapping the button twice does not email every administrator twice.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

**Use case:** observability for the Authorize+Capture path — clients can show reserved-vs-debited credits, audit recently released holds, and reconcile their local view of the user's balance.

Retrieve the authenticated user's balance movements — credits and service charges — newest first.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`

post.description:
Receive transaction status updates from the payment service. This endpoint carries no Bearer authentication and is invoked by the external payment provider. The provider does NOT sign its callbacks, so authenticity rests on a shared secret that 1Platform generates and an operator installs on the provider side; the provider returns it as an `X-Webhook-Token` header or a `?token=` query parameter. Verification is fail-closed (401) only while `payments.webhook_auth_enforced` is true; until that cutover the endpoint accepts unverified callbacks and merely logs the verdict the check would have reached. Processing is idempotent — duplicate webhooks are safely ignored to prevent double-charging — and the endpoint always returns HTTP 200 to suppress aggressive provider retries. Rate limit: 20 req/min.

**Flow:**
1. Extract `externalId` from the root payload to find the local transaction
2. Check idempotency (if status unchanged, return success)
3. Validate status transition
4. Update transaction status
5. If approved, credit the user's balance

**Response format** (simple JSON, not ResponseWrapper):
```json
{"status": "success", "message": "Processed"}
```

200.description: Webhook processed (or safely ignored if duplicate)

401.description: Missing or invalid webhook token. Only returned while `payments.webhook_auth_enforced` is true.

Partially update a business (`name`, `address`, `status`, `defaultBranchId`).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Accessible to the business owner or an `app_admin` of the same tenant
- `defaultBranchId` designates the branch that issues invoices created **without** `branchId`. Set it and an integration that never sends a branch keeps working after the business configures its establishment codes; leave it unset and such a request answers `422` `branch_selection_required`. It must name a branch of this business (`404` if unknown, `400` if it belongs to another), and an explicit `null` clears it — the only field on this schema where null means something. It stays editable on a business whose `name`/`address` are already frozen: it is not part of the fiscal identity
- **Fiscal identity is immutable:** `documentNumber` and `documentType` are not part of this schema. Invoices were already certified against that tax id, so changing it would desynchronise them — sending either field returns `422`
- Setting `status` to `inactive` deactivates the business; invoices already issued are not altered

delete.description:
Remove a business from the workspace by archiving it.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Requires the `admin` role on the business (or being an `app_admin` of its tenant)
- **Nothing is deleted.** The business is marked archived and every related document is preserved: invoices already certified, branches, user assignments, payment links, deliveries and terminal applications. Its invoices keep appearing in `GET /invoices` and in the tax report
- The business disappears from `GET /businesses` and `GET /admin/businesses`, stops accepting writes, and its `GET /businesses/{businessId}` still answers 200 with `archived: true` so a saved link can explain what happened
- Idempotent: archiving an already-archived business answers 200 and keeps the original timestamp
- The document number stays taken by the archived business; creating a new one with it answers 409 `business_nit_archived`
- **Payment links are NOT switched off unless you ask.** The public checkout resolves a link by its token and never loads the business, so a link issued before archiving stays payable. Pass `cancel_payment_links=true` to cancel the ones still charging; the response then carries `payment_links_cancelled` with what actually happened. Without the parameter the behaviour is unchanged
- `data.active_payment_links` reports the links still charging (`{count, totals}` per currency), so the caller can warn before archiving

post.description:
Issue a new invoice for a business via electronic invoicing (FEL).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- The invoice is associated directly to the business (via business_id)
- The business NIT is used as the emitter for FEL invoicing
- **Which branch issues it:** send `branchId` and the invoice is attributed to that branch and certified under its FEL establishment. Omit it and the server resolves the branch: the only one, or the one the business designated as `defaultBranchId` (`PATCH /businesses/{businessId}`). With several branches, no designation and at least one establishment code configured, the request is refused with `422` and `code: branch_selection_required` — the response's `data.branches` lists the ids to retry with. Nothing is emitted on that refusal and no FEL correlative is consumed

**Flow:**
1. Authenticate and resolve businessId from the path
2. Validate business exists
3. Validate invoice items and receptorInfo
4. Persist invoice associated to business_id
5. If `emitOnCreate=true`, emit via FEL using the business NIT

Nothing is ever deleted or deactivated, and a branch whose establishment was set by hand is left alone.

Safe to run repeatedly: establishments are matched by their code, so a second run creates nothing new.

Requires the business to have finished invoicing activation. Reports what it created, updated, left unchanged and skipped — and warns when the business now has enough branches that issuing an invoice must state which one it comes from.

A `null` in place of a namespace removes the namespace; a `null` in place of a setting removes that setting. Only `billing`, `pricing`, `limits` and `features` are writable, and of `billing` only `enabled`.

Deactivating the tenant you are authenticated with is refused, and so is deactivating an administrative tenant. There is **no delete**: the logical removal of a tenant is `status: inactive`.

get.description:
Every knob of the advertising vertical with its **effective** value and the level it came from (`app` / `platform` / `default`).

The origin is the point: `300` does not tell an operator whether the tenant was configured or is merely inheriting, and switching `enabled` on for a tenant whose category or funding range still resolves to `platform` is how a bakery's ad gets filed under the wrong regulated category.

The provider credential appears as a **boolean**, never as a value.

patch.summary: Write one tenant's ads configuration override (superadmin)
patch.description:
Writes `App.config["ads"]` for the tenant named in the path. Takes effect on the **next request** — the tenant's App is re-read per request, so this is the live rollback lever for the vertical.

Keys outside the allow-list are **422**, not a silent assignment: the generic `App.config` patch accepts anything, and for a namespace that governs a third party's spending ceilings that is how a typo becomes a permanent invisible setting. Values are range-checked, and the money ceilings cannot be raised above the platform's own — an override may only reduce exposure.

The tenant cannot reach this: `ads` is in `_PROTECTED_CONFIG_KEYS`, so `PATCH /admin/app` answers **400** for this namespace.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>` (superadmin)

Unlike the Search Console key — which is the tenant's own — this credential belongs to the **platform**: the ad account is the platform's (D-4), so the tenant is not its owner and cannot write it.

The response carries a **boolean**, never the value, and the request body is redacted before it reaches `ApiLog`.

Fields omitted from the body are left untouched; fields sent as `null` are cleared, falling back to the platform default.

post.description:
The manual exit from `failed`, and the reason the rule "never auto-resolve an unknown money outcome" is survivable rather than a way to freeze a user's balance for ever.

The verdict is a STATEMENT of what was established, not a hint: `not_captured` releases the reservation, `captured` closes the cycle without touching the balance, `not_credited` pays the settlement, `credited` closes it. Who resolved it, with which verdict and with what note is written to the log.

get.summary: Which switchable features each tenant has on (superadmin)
get.description:
The tenant × feature matrix, with the effective value and — the point of the screen — **where it came from**. Today no tenant in production has any of these keys written, so every one of them is inheriting and nothing surfaces that.

`operable` answers whether the vertical's provider-backed path can run right now. A feature can legitimately be `enabled: true, operable: false`: switching it on before contracting the provider is a normal order of operations, and the vertical answers its own typed error until then.

This response is a **projection**. It never carries `App.config`, which holds tenant mail credentials in plain text.

⚠️ `source: "platform"` reflects the `PlatformSettings` snapshot taken at boot: `ConfigProvider` loads it once, so a value edited straight in Mongo shows up here only after a restart.

⚠️ `enforcement` is the one field to read before trusting a switch. Only `ads` resolves the tenant's own App, so only its switch blocks that tenant's users. `deliveries` and `trading` gate on `current_app.config` — the App of the BEARER TOKEN — so switching either off for a tenant that is not the caller's own App removes the module from that tenant's menu and blocks nothing server-side.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>` (superadmin)

patch.summary: Switch one feature on or off for one tenant (superadmin)
patch.description:
Writes the single leaf `App.config.<namespace>.enabled` with a targeted `$set`, so a vertical's other settings — spending ceilings, provider, windows — are left exactly as they are.

Three operations, not two:

- `{"enabled": true}` switches on
- `{"enabled": false}` switches off **explicitly** (`source` becomes `app`)
- `{"enabled": null}` **removes** the override so the tenant inherits again

An empty body is **422**: a request that says nothing must not read as a successful change.

The tenant cannot undo this. Every namespace in the catalogue is in `_PROTECTED_CONFIG_KEYS`, so `PATCH /admin/app` answers 400 for it.

⚠️ The switch is per **App**, and `GET /dashboard/bootstrap` resolves the App of the *token*, not of the user — so flipping a feature on the App the dashboard front-end itself authenticates with reaches every one of its users at once.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>` (superadmin)

**Auth:** tenant `app_admin` role required.
**Rate limit:** 10/hour per caller.

1Platform has no passwords, so 'create a user' means: create the account, grant it the roles, and send the link. Distinct from `POST /users/invite`, which merely re-sends a link and is idempotent — this one is a `409` if the address is already registered.

- An email already registered — **in any tenant** — is a `409` with a deliberately generic message, and NO email is sent.
- If the email cannot be delivered, the link is invalidated and the call answers `503`: a 2xx would let the caller lift the token from the response and walk in as the new user.

WHOSE ``App.config`` the vertical's own server-side gate reads.

Not a nicety — it is the difference between a switch and a label.

switching the feature off for a tenant blocks that tenant's users. Only
``ads`` does this today (``endpoints/ads.py::_tenant_config``).

TOKEN, which for every dashboard user is the ``dashboard`` app rather than
their own tenant (``endpoints/deliveries.py``, ``endpoints/trading.py``).
Switching such a feature off for some *other* tenant removes its menu entry
(``GET /dashboard/modules`` IS per tenant) and does **not** block anything
server-side. The console says so rather than implying an enforcement it does
not have; making it true means changing where two live money verticals
resolve their config, which is a different epic.

since ``enabled=None`` is both the default and a meaningful value. The
trading config patch next door already carries the same machinery for the
same reason.

assert its exact value, so it has to travel on the wire even though the
plan's abbreviated example body omits it. Defaults to ``"poll"``, the
routine background case, so an old plugin build that never sends it
still gets a truthful source.

UpdateBranchRequest.title: UpdateBranchRequest
UpdateBranchRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /businesses/{businessId}/branches/{branchId}``.

Three independent patchable concerns, all optional: the display ``name``,
the pickup block (deliveries) and the FEL establishment code (fiscal
identity, EST-01/D-4). A request must carry at least one —
``extra="forbid"`` keeps a typo (or an attempt to rewrite ``commerceId``)
a loud 422 instead of a silent no-op, but it does NOT reject an empty body,
and it does NOT reject an explicit ``null`` on a known optional field. Both
of those are handled below.

``name`` is added by fel-sincronizar-establecimientos (SES-02). Until then a
branch could be named ONCE, at creation, and never again: this DTO had no
``name`` field and ``extra="forbid"`` rejected it, so `Branch.name` had
exactly one writer in the whole codebase. That made the establishment sync
unshippable as approved — the sync OVERWRITES the name the business typed
with the one the registry declares, and the user approved that overwrite on
the stated premise that they could "rename the branch again whenever they
want" (requerimiento P-2, and an acceptance criterion of SES-02). Without a
write path that premise was false and the overwrite was irreversible.

This is the display label only. It is NOT the fiscal identity: that lives in
``establishment_code`` and in the registry's own ``fel_commercial_name`` /
``fel_address``, which the sync keeps separately and which this endpoint
cannot touch. Contrast ``BusinessService.LOCKED_FIELDS``, which freezes a
*business* name and address once registered with the tax authority — those
ARE the fiscal identity, a branch's display name is not.

``establishment_code`` is declared ``strict`` on purpose: Pydantic's lax
mode would coerce the string ``"2"`` into ``2`` and we would forward it
happily, but the emitter's contract requires a JSON **number** and answers
400 to a string. Failing here makes that a 422 the caller can act on,
instead of a 400 three layers down whose message we do not own.

defaultBranchId.title: Defaultbranchid
defaultBranchId.description: Branch that issues invoices created without `branchId` (EST-06). Must be a branch of THIS business. Unlike every other field here, an explicit `null` CLEARS the designation instead of meaning 'leave unchanged' — the field is nullable by design (the other three back required columns, where null would brick the row), so 'no default branch' has to be expressible or the merchant could designate one and never take it back. Omit the key to leave it untouched.

UpdateBusinessRequest.title: UpdateBusinessRequest
UpdateBusinessRequest.description:
Partial update of a business. Fiscal identity is immutable.

`documentNumber` / `documentType` are absent BY CONTRACT: invoices were
already certified against that NIT with the FEL provider, so changing it
would desynchronise them. `extra="forbid"` is what turns "absent from the
schema" into an actual 422 — Pydantic's default silently ignores unknown

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Referral program lookups — resolve a referral code to its public metadata (program name, signup URL, app branding).

tags.name: User Authentication
tags.description: Passwordless dashboard login — request a magic link, exchange it for an access + refresh token pair, rotate refresh tokens, and revoke sessions on logout.

tags.name: Platform Admin
tags.description: Cross-tenant administration for the 1Platform team — provision new apps, list every registered app, inspect a single app, and view platform-wide metrics. Requires the superadmin role.

tags.name: Tenant Admin
tags.description: Per-tenant administration scoped to the actor's `app_id`. Lets the tenant `app_admin` role list/manage users, roles and impersonation, plus read business, invoicing, billing, domain and operational data for their own tenant.

tags.name: Provisioning
tags.description: One-click asynchronous provisioning of new Atlas tenants (dashboard + app) for a domain. The `app_admin` role starts a job and polls its progress; every resource is scoped to the caller's own workspace (`app_id`), so a cross-tenant job id returns 404 without leaking its existence.

tags.name: API Developer
tags.description: A caller's own API credentials. Several may exist at once, each revocable on its own, and the secret is returned exactly once — at the moment it is issued. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so there is no endpoint that can show it again; a lost credential is replaced, not recovered. Disabling or deleting one cuts it off on the next request, including for a token already issued from it and still inside its expiry window.

tags.name: API Developer (admin)
tags.description: The tenant administrator's view of the same credentials: who holds what, when each was last exchanged, and the ability to cut any of them the moment one leaks. No response on this surface ever carries a secret — not by filtering, but because the only two endpoints that return one belong to the credential's owner. The workspace credential refuses being disabled or deleted: the front-ends carry it compiled into their bundle, so cutting it would sign every user of the tenant out at once. Rotating it is the supported path.

tags.name: Trading
tags.description:
1Trade: turn part of your balance into an automated position that buys at a market amount and sells at a higher one, optionally repeating and compounding the realised result.

Creating a trade RESERVES the amount; the balance only moves against a confirmed fill, and what comes back is the amount really received net of fees — never the theoretical target. The result is credited as 1Platform balance and is not withdrawable.

tags.name: Trading Agent
tags.description:
The surface a 1Trade monitor uses. Authenticated with a service credential alone (`Authorization: Bearer ak-svc-…`) carrying the `trade.execute` capability and platform scope — no app token and no user token.

The monitor decides **when** to look at a cycle. The server decides what, how much and whether: it derives the action from the cycle's own state, re-reads the price itself, and re-checks the trigger. The request body carries no action, no reason and no amount.

tags.name: Activation
tags.description:
Receives paid activation purchases from the storefront that sells the activation package.

**Not part of the two-token model.** The caller is another product and holds no 1Platform credentials, so the HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw request body is the credential (`X-Bowerbird-Signature` plus `X-Bowerbird-Timestamp`, which bounds replay).

Delivery is retried, so the endpoint is idempotent on `event_key`: a repeat answers 200 and changes nothing. The amount of balance a purchase is worth is resolved from the platform's package catalogue and never read from the request body.
